summary: Lenalidomide is an oral thalidomide-analogue immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) for multiple myeloma (with dexamethasone and as post-transplant maintenance), del(5q) myelodysplastic syndrome, relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma, and previously treated follicular and marginal zone lymphoma (with rituximab). It carries a BOXED WARNING for embryo-fetal toxicity (a thalidomide analogue, a known human teratogen), hematologic toxicity (neutropenia/thrombocytopenia), and venous/arterial thromboembolism, and is available only through the restricted Lenalidomide REMS program.

moa: Lenalidomide is a thalidomide analogue with immunomodulatory, antiangiogenic, and antineoplastic properties. Its actions are mediated through binding the protein cereblon, a component of a cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase complex; this targets substrate proteins (including Aiolos, Ikaros, and CK1-alpha) for ubiquitination and degradation, producing direct cytotoxic and immunomodulatory effects. It inhibits proliferation and induces apoptosis of certain hematopoietic tumor cells, increases the number/activation of T and NK cells (enhancing antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity via IL-2 and IFN-gamma), and inhibits pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6).

monitor: Tumor lysis / tumor flare in lymphoma

preg: CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy. Lenalidomide is a thalidomide analogue; thalidomide is a known human teratogen causing severe, life-threatening birth defects (amelia, phocomelia, bone hypoplasia, ear/eye abnormalities, congenital heart defects). Obtain 2 negative pregnancy tests before starting. Females of reproductive potential must use 2 forms of contraception (>=1 highly effective) or abstain during and for 4 weeks after treatment. A pregnancy exposure registry exists; report exposures to the REMS Call Center (1-888-423-5436) and FDA MedWatch.
lact: Advise patients not to breastfeed during treatment with lenalidomide because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant.
renal: Lenalidomide is substantially excreted by the kidney; reduce the starting dose based on creatinine clearance (separate adjustments for CrCl 30-60 mL/min, <30 mL/min not on dialysis, and dialysis). On dialysis days, give the dose after dialysis.
hepatic: Hepatic failure, including fatalities, has occurred. Monitor liver function; stop lenalidomide and evaluate if hepatotoxicity is suspected. Treatment may be restarted at a lower dose after return to baseline.

major: Erythropoietin-stimulating agents and estrogen-containing therapies — increased risk of thrombosis (use only after benefit-risk assessment)
Pembrolizumab added to a thalidomide analogue + dexamethasone in MM — increased mortality (not recommended)
moderate: Digoxin — lenalidomide increases digoxin Cmax/AUC ~14%; monitor digoxin levels
minor: Warfarin — no PK interaction, but monitor PT/INR per standard practice
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food (a high-fat meal lowers Cmax ~50% and AUC ~20%, but it is given without regard to food).
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC frequently, liver function, thyroid function, and (where applicable) tumor lysis parameters.

pearls: BOXED WARNINGS: embryo-fetal toxicity (thalidomide analogue), hematologic toxicity (neutropenia/thrombocytopenia), and venous/arterial thromboembolism
Available only through the restricted Lenalidomide REMS program (formerly RevAssist) — prescribers, pharmacies, and patients must be certified
Thromboprophylaxis (aspirin or anticoagulation) is recommended, especially in MM with dexamethasone
Two negative pregnancy tests before starting and ongoing monthly testing are mandatory in females of reproductive potential
Reduce starting dose in renal impairment; lenalidomide is renally cleared

missed: If a dose is missed and it is within 12 hours of the scheduled time, take it; if more than 12 hours have passed, skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific experience with lenalidomide overdose in patients. In studies up to 200 mg/day and single 400 mg doses, pruritus, urticaria, rash, and elevated transaminases were the main adverse effects; the dose-limiting toxicity is neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Provide supportive care and monitor blood counts and liver function.
